Welcome to Fledglings Pre-School
The Best Start
"Children in early years settle quickly into the school’s routines and learn well together." Ofsted January 2024
The main aim of our pre-school, Fledglings (2 to 3 years) and Nursery (3 to 4 year) is to provide a setting where the children feel emotionally safe and secure. The environment is friendly, nurturing and stimulating and the curriculum is based around the Early Years Foundation Scheme (EYFS) framework.
We are proud that we are a Let's Talk Together accredited setting, recognised as providing an exemplary environment for children to develop good speech, language and communication skills within an emotionally connected approach.
Our wonderful pre-school provides a warm and welcoming environment. In a small friendly setting, with a fantastic core team of practitioners; our children benefit from fun child-led activities and great teaching. Three-hour sessions, either morning or afternoon, are available for 2 and 3 year olds.
For further information, please see:

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Sparrow Farm Primary School and what a joy and privilege it is to be part of this fantastic school and community. You will have heard about our vision of shaping the future of our remarkable children whilst holding true to our values: to be ambitious, bold and curious.
The beating heart of Sparrow Farm is our pupils and staff. Together, we bring teaching and learning to LIFE by offering Learning Inspired by Fulfilling Experiences. The curriculum is innovative and engaging, and everything you would expect from a forward-thinking, aspirational school. We have a thematic approach to teaching which enables our children to make connections in their education by ‘learning more, remembering more’.
Our model for learning, built on increasing pupils’ motivation, is enriched by real experiences and purposeful play. We focus relentlessly on an holistic approach of teaching and learning, and preparing our pupils for life. We are privileged that you have entrusted us with the most important and rewarding responsibility of educating and looking after the academic, physical, social, emotional and spiritual welfare of your child.
We are committed to learning and working with other schools and we are proud to belong to Hounslow Education Partnership. We are trailblazers within Hounslow with our family-focused Relationship Policy which has been a catalyst for change in the way in which other schools support children's emotional wellbeing.
Each individual pupil and member of staff at Sparrow Farm Primary School is unique. Our aspiration is to develop each and every one to be a confident, successful, lifelong learner, who is prepared and excited to grasp the opportunities ahead of them with courage and determination.
We relish the opportunity of playing our part in building a better world within our community and beyond. Our embrace and warm welcome extends to all families and our community; we value each other and what we have, and can, achieve collectively.
Come and join us on this wonderful journey of exploration and innovation within the family here at Sparrow Farm Primary School.
Why Join Us?

pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Nursery
The Early Years Matter!
"Children in early years settle quickly into the school’s routines and learn well together." Ofsted January 2024
Embedded in our teaching, are the school’s values of Ambitious, Bold and Curious. Through the Early Years framework we strive to inspire and nurture in your child these strongly held values to ensure the children’s experiences in Nursery are enriched. We confidently grow to meet and succeed in rapidly changing times and the preservation of our planet and good health.
At Sparrow Farm Primary School we believe in facilitating and supporting the development of the whole-child, and in Nursery follow the Government’s statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework. This guidance carefully takes into account childrens’ natural steps, or ‘milestones’ as they are sometimes known, in their growth and how we as professionals can observe, assess and plan to meet each individual’s needs. Children are like sponges and soak up every experience provided to them. These early years are crucial to laying the foundation in your child’s education and their future achievements and wellbeing.
The EYFS is split between Prime Areas and Specific Areas of learning. Each is sequential to the next and by the end of year Reception, between 40-60 months in age range, your child is expected to reach and be embedding the 17 Early Learning Goals.
You are very welcome to come and visit our Nursery to see the brilliant learning and excitement for yourselves.
To arrange an appointment please contact the school office: admissions@sparrowfarm.hounslow.sch.uk or phone 020 8890 7194 option 3.
Why Join Us?

Personal, Social and Health and Economic Education
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education is a subject through which pupils develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to manage their lives, now and in the future. It helps children and young people to stay healthy and safe, while preparing them to make the most of life and work (PSHE Association)
At Sparrow Farm Primary School we aim to deliver a PSHE curriculum that is accessible to all. Through weekly PSHE sessions, and focused events our aim is for our pupils to become responsible, independent, healthy and confident members of the school society as well the wider society.
We want our children to feel confident enough to tackle any issues that may arise including moral, social and cultural ones. Our children are supported to develop their sense of self which will in turn enable them to be a positive role model to others.
Our PSHE curriculum at Sparrow Farm Primary School has five core areas:
(In Year 6 an additional area of ‘Identity’ is covered)
We use KAPOW planning and resources to support the delivery of Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and PSHE. The scheme covers wider PSHE learning, in line with the requirement of the National curriculum (2014) that schools "should make provision for personal, social, health and economic education (PSHE)". Children’s learning through this scheme significantly contributes to their personal development as set out in the Ofsted Inspection Framework and promotes the four fundamental British values which reflect life in modern Britain:
At Sparrow Farm Primary School we are aware that the delivered curriculum must reflect the needs of our pupils, so although we use documents from the PSHE Association to support us in our planning, class teachers also take into account the needs of their individual pupils and will adapt the curriculum to address any issues or concerns that may arise during the course of the year.
Through delivering our PSHE curriculum we aim for the children to leave us in Year 6 as healthy, happy and responsible members of society.

PE and Sport Premium
Physical activity has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health and mental wellbeing (increasing self-esteem and emotional wellbeing and lowering anxiety and depression). Children who are physically active are happier, more resilient and more trusting of their peers.
The PE and Sport Premium is a grant allocated to schools to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the PE, physical activity and sport offered through schools' core budgets. It is allocated directly to schools, so we have the flexibility to use it in the way that works best for our pupils.

Music
At Sparrow Farm Primary, we believe children are naturally curious young musical creators who are enthusiastic and confident to develop their own musical sense. As renowned American musician John Finney says, “Music is in our bones!” They are open, reflective and adaptive to a wide variety of genres, and use their drive to sing and create their own music. Music is incorporated in everything we do; it is a language, art, our well-being and feeds into all areas of the curriculum.
Music is taught using a range of resources, which allows the children to gain a wide variety of musical experiences within a range of genres. Charanga's original scheme is taught from Nursery to Year 2 and from Year 3 children are taught a hybrid curriculum which is taught through Charanga by music specialists in partnership with Hounslow Music Service. This allows all pupils to learn a range of tuned instruments during their time at Sparrow Farm.
Through Yumu (Charanga’s supplementary online resource) all children are able to access digital composition software from home as well as being able to access a range of online musical resources relevant to their in-school lessons. Additionally, Rocksteady provide an additional resource for some students to help develop their confidence to perform in assemblies.
Our music lessons give clear visuals, using ICT, which are engaging, and ensure that the children are active. The scheme builds on skills and musical knowledge at an age appropriate level. Teachers also record assessments onto Charanga and children can tap into Music online to consolidate their learning and interests through Yumu.
Singing assemblies, Rocksteady, and productions throughout the year also allow the children to enhance their music ability and build confidence in their developing musical techniques to perform in front of an audience.
The school also believes that Music is important to children’s wellbeing and happiness, as well as understanding and appreciating different types of genres, history and culture associated with each piece of Music.
The BBC's Ten Pieces opens up the world of classical music to 7-14 year olds. with exciting films, lesson plans, instrumental arrangements & live events!

Our Governors
Membership, Tenure & Attendance
School Governors are members of a school’s Governing Board; they have responsibility for raising school standards through their three key roles of setting strategic direction, ensuring accountability and acting as a critical friend.
Here at Sparrow Farm Primary School the Governing Board consists of governors from differing areas,
Whether appointed or elected each governor has a term of office, which is a maximum of four years before they have to seek re-election/re-appointment.
All Governors are appointed or elected in accordance with the Instrument of Government and under the guidance of the Local Authority representative. All appointments are recorded in the Full Governing Board Minutes.
Being a Governor is voluntary and as such, Governors do not receive any payment for their work. Training is given for every aspect of the role and is delivered locally by the local authority, through specialist on-line training packages and through national organisations.
The Governing Board meet termly. Governors reviewed their Committee structure in January 2023 and moved to a flat structure with only a Pay Committee. The Governing Board agree Terms of Reference for the full Governing Board and Pay Committee each year.
Current members of the Governing Board are:
Parents – elected by other parents.
Co-opted – appointed by the governing body.

Attendance
Attendance and the Importance of Being in School
At Sparrow Farm Primary School, we know that every day in school really does make a difference.
Good attendance helps children:
Build confidence and independence
Develop lasting friendships
When children miss school, even for a short time, it can be harder for them to catch up with lessons and routines.
We ask all parents and carers to support us by ensuring children attend school every day and arrive on time, ready to learn.
Make the most of their learning

Where possible, please make medical and dental appointments outside school hours.
Term-Time Leave
By law, children must attend school regularly. The Headteacher can only authorise term-time leave in exceptional circumstances. This means that holidays, family visits, or extended trips overseas will not be approved.
Please note that medical treatment overseas cannot be authorised, as suitable treatment can be arranged in the UK.
If you need to request time off during term time, please complete a Leave of Absence Request Form before making any travel arrangements. Each request will be carefully considered, but approval will only be given in exceptional cases.
Absence Due to Illness
If your child is unwell, please let the school office know as soon as possible each morning they are absent. You can leave a message on 02088907194, or email attendance@sparrowfarm.hounslow.sch.uk
Please be aware that any absence immediately before or after a school holiday will be recorded as unauthorised unless supported by medical evidence, even if the absence is reported as illness.
Working Together for Good Attendance
We understand that there may be times when your child’s attendance is affected by illness or family difficulties. If you are finding it hard to get your child into school, please talk to us — we are here to help and support your family.
Together, we can make sure every child enjoys their learning, feels part of the school community, and reaches their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sparrow Farm Primary School - School Lunch and Milk
pageCache.text:
School Lunch and Milk
School Lunch
All children at Sparrow Farm Primary School are able to have a free, healthy, hot meal at lunchtime, which is cooked on site by our catering partners PS Catering.
The meal selection should be booked via Scopay. Please contact the school office if you need any help.
PS Catering
School Milk
By registering your child for our school milk scheme they will receive a 189 ml (a third of a pint) carton of semi-skimmed milk every day. This is delivered fresh and chilled to their classroom.
How much does it cost?
Thanks to government subsidies, school milk is free for all under-fives and is subsidised for children aged five or older (payable online to Cool Milk).
Why should I register my child?
School milk provides your child with essential nutrients such as calcium and protein, for strong, healthy teeth and bones. It is also rehydrating and energy boosting, helping to bridge the long gap between breakfast and lunch so children stay focused.
How do I register my child?
If your child is under five
If your child is over five
For more information visit www.coolmilk.com or contact Cool Milk directly on 0844 854 2913.
